pricing.summary: T-001 (Artic 44t Curtain Side, HGV) ran a two-leg chained day from Peckham SE15: load 91100009 Peckham→Nottingham (£740) then load 91105108 Nottingham→Reading (£440), returning empty from Reading to Peckham. Revenue £1,180, cost £802.05, profit £377.95 over 315.3 miles (51.6 empty miles, 16.4% empty ratio), 8.05 drive hours, one 45-minute break, max continuous 4.5h, home at 19:21. Baseline (empty return from Nottingham) was £65.26 profit with 139.2 empty miles and home at 16:13, so the chained plan added £312.69 profit, cut empty miles by 87.6, and cost 3h08m later home time. At the 12:01 decision point in STANDARD mode the engine auto-booked 91105108 (Reading, £440, net_load £94.62, margin 21.5%) over the empty-return alternative (net −£313.20, home 16:13), an uplift of £298.74. A higher-paying Southampton load (91105195, £600, net £137.22) was correctly rejected as infeasible on OUT_OF_HOURS (10.3h driving needed vs 9.0h cap) and HOME_DEADLINE (21:48 vs 21:00 limit) — the 'tempting_illegal' extra £42.60 was not taken. At 18:09 in HOMEWARD mode the engine drove home empty (net −£109.08, home 19:21) because all four evaluated loads (Leeds £610, Manchester £480, Leeds £470, Manchester £450) failed on VEHICLE_MISMATCH, DEADHEAD_TOO_FAR, WINDOW_MISSED, BELOW_MARGIN_FLOOR, OUT_OF_HOURS, HOME_DEADLINE and MOVES_AWAY_FROM_HOME. Diesel at 198.8p/l is the main cost driver and is at the upper end of cited UK averages (197.6–199.3p/l), so fuel cost assumptions are conservative. The only restriction evidence is an expired (published 05/02/26) TfL traffic order for Peckham High Street resurfacing, which does not affect the current plan.
risk_flags: HOMEWARD_LEG_NEGATIVE: the final 48.1-mile empty return from Reading to Peckham is priced at net −£109.08; the day's profit depends entirely on the two booked loads covering it.

LATE_HOME_TIME: home at 19:21 versus baseline 16:13 — the chained plan consumes 3h08m of additional driver time for £312.69 extra profit, and leaves only ~1h39m before the 21:00 home deadline, so any Reading-side delay would push the return into the HOME_DEADLINE gate.

TIGHT_HAULIAGE_CAP_HEADROOM: the Southampton option needed 10.3h driving against a 9.0h cap and would have landed at 21:48 vs a 21:00 limit — only ~£42.60 of extra rate was available for a clear compliance breach, so the margin between legal and illegal was narrow.

MARGIN_FLOOR_BINDING: every rejected load at 18:09 was also below the 8% margin floor (−1% to −49%), meaning the rejections were not purely compliance-driven; the empty return was the only feasible option regardless of hours.

DEADHEAD_LIMIT_CONSTRAINT: the 30-mile max deadhead rule excluded all four 18:09 loads (47–52 mi) and the Norwich/Cardiff options (54–57 mi) at 12:01, so the search space was heavily constrained by deadhead distance rather than by rate.
EMPTY_MILE_RATIO_STILL_NONZERO: 51.6 of 315.3 miles (16.4%) were empty (1.0 + 2.5 deadhead plus 48.1 empty home leg), so the plan is not fully back-to-back.

FUEL_PRICE_SENSITIVITY: diesel at 198.8p/l sits at the top of the cited 197.6–199.3p/l range and ~40% above the year-earlier 142.8p/l; a further rise would erode the £377.95 profit, and the 21.5% margin on the Reading leg is the thinnest buffer on the chosen loads.

RESTRICTION_EVIDENCE_STALE: the only traffic notice (Peckham High Street, SE15 5EW) is marked Expired and dated 05/02/26, so no current local restriction is confirmed for the home area; the restriction_summary field is effectively non-actionable.
WAIT_TIME_UNPRODUCTIVE: 16 minutes of wait at 06:49 and 33 minutes at 12:12 (49 min total) plus 45 min load and 45 min unload each — non-driving time is a material share of the 12h36m shift.
SINGLE_VEHICLE_SINGLE_DRIVER: one truck and one driver (DRV-001) with no redundancy; any breakdown, detention or load-window slip on the Nottingham→Reading leg has no fallback in the plan.

compliance.summary: T-001 (Artic 44t Curtain Side, HGV) ran a two-leg chained day from Peckham SE15: load 91100009 Peckham→Nottingham (£740) then load 91105108 Nottingham→Reading (£440), returning home empty to Peckham at 19:21. Total revenue £1,180, cost £802.05, profit £377.95 over 315.3 miles (51.6 empty miles, 16.4% empty ratio), 8.05 driving hours with one 45-minute break and a maximum continuous driving stint of 4.5h. The 12:01 STANDARD decision auto-booked 91105108 (Reading) over the empty-return baseline, adding £298.74 uplift; the higher-paying 91105195 to Southampton (£600, +£42.6) was correctly rejected as infeasible on OUT_OF_HOURS (10.3h driving needed vs 9.0h cap) and HOME_DEADLINE (21:48 vs 21:00 limit). The 18:09 HOMEWARD decision drove home empty rather than taking any of four offered loads, all of which were correctly flagged infeasible (vehicle mismatch, deadhead distance, missed windows, negative margin, out-of-hours, home deadline, moving away from home). Baseline comparison shows profit up from £65.26 to £377.95 and empty miles down from 139.2 to 51.6, with home arrival 19:21 versus 16:13 baseline. All compliance gates appear to have been applied as designed and no booking, hour, or gate was altered.
risk_flags: DRIVING_HOURS_HEADROOM: 8.05h total driving against a 9.0h cap leaves only ~0.95h of remaining daily driving capacity; the Southampton option was rejected on this basis, so the day is close to the daily limit and any delay or extra leg would breach it.
HOME_DEADLINE_MARGIN: home at 19:21 versus a 21:00 limit gives ~1h39m of slack; the rejected Southampton load would have arrived 21:48, i.e. 48 minutes past the deadline.

MAX_CONTINUOUS_DRIVING: 4.5h maximum continuous stint is at the stated limit, so the single 45-minute break at 14:18-15:03 is the only separator between the two Reading driving segments; any extension of the 15:03-17:24 segment would breach the continuous limit.
BREAK_COUNT_MARGIN: only 1 break recorded across 8.05h driving; the EU/UK 4.5h rule requires a break after each 4.5h block, so there is no spare break in the schedule if the first block is extended.

EMPTY_MILES_STILL_PRESENT: 51.6 empty miles (16.4% of 315.3) remain, including 1.0 mi home-to-pickup, 2.5 mi Nottingham deadhead and 48.1 mi empty return from Reading to Peckham; the Reading leg is a net-to-home loss (-£14.46) and was only justified by the £298.74 uplift versus the empty-return baseline.

LATE_HOME_VS_BASELINE: home at 19:21 is 3h08m later than the 16:13 baseline, reducing driver rest before the next shift; the 06:45 departure the following day leaves only ~11h24m rest, which is below the 11h daily rest minimum if the same pattern repeats.

MARGIN_FLOOR_NEAR_ZERO: the chosen Reading load has a 21.5% load margin but a net-to-home of -£14.46, so the leg is only viable because of the chained-load uplift; a small rate or fuel movement would push it below the 8% margin floor.

RESTRICTION_NOTICE_EXPIRED: the only traffic restriction cited (TfL A202 Peckham High Street, SE15 5EW) is marked 'Published 05/02/26 - Expired', so it imposes no current constraint on the Peckham pickup or return; it should not be treated as an active gate.

FUEL_PRICE_SOURCE_VARIANCE: diesel is quoted at 198.8p/l in the market data while cited sources range 197.58p-199.33p; the cost model is sensitive to this input and the citation set is not fully consistent with the headline figure.

DECISION_TRACE_INCOMPLETE: only 2 of 273 evaluated options at 12:01 and 2 of 93 at 18:09 are shown in the trace, so the full option set and the basis for the AUTO_BOOK ranking cannot be independently verified from the evidence provided.

NO_REPORTED_BREAK_AFTER_FIRST_LEG: the 07:50-11:16 Nottingham drive is 3h26m and the 13:30-14:18 segment is 48m, but no break is recorded between the 11:16 unload and the 13:30 load; the 33-minute wait at 12:12-12:45 may or may not qualify as a rest period under the rules applied.

NO_ULRZ_CHARGE_APPLIED: ulez_charge_gbp is 0.0, which is consistent with a 44t articulated HGV operating outside the London ULEZ chargeable class, but the evidence does not explicitly confirm the vehicle's ULEZ status for the SE15 movements.

fleet-fit.summary: T-001 (Artic 44t Curtain Side, driver DRV-001) ran a two-leg chained day from Peckham SE15: load 91100009 Peckham→Nottingham (£740) then load 91105108 Nottingham→Reading (£440), returning empty from Reading. The plan departs home at 06:45 and is back at 19:21, with 315.3 miles total (51.6 empty), 8.05 driving hours, one 45-minute break at 14:18–15:03, and max continuous driving of 4.5h. Revenue £1,180 against costs £802.05 gives profit £377.95, versus a baseline of £65.26 profit with 139.2 empty miles and a 16:13 home time — so the plan adds £312.69 profit, cuts empty miles by 87.6, and brings the driver home 3h08m earlier. At the 12:01 decision point in Nottingham the dispatcher ran STANDARD mode and auto-booked 91105108 to Reading (£440, net load £94.62, 21.5% margin), which beat the empty-return alternative (net £-313.20, home 16:13) by £298.74. At 18:09 in Reading, HOMEWARD mode correctly chose DRIVE_HOME_EMPTY (net £-109.08, home 19:21) because every available load was infeasible on multiple gates. The plan is deterministic and no bookings, hours, or compliance gates were altered.
risk_flags: Tempting-illegal load 91105195 (Nottingham→Southampton, £600) was correctly rejected: OUT_OF_HOURS (10.3h driving needed vs 9.0h cap) and HOME_DEADLINE (21:48 vs 21:00 limit). It would have added only £42.60, so the compliance gates cost little here.
Longest continuous driving block is 4.5h (07:50–11:16, 137.6 miles loaded to Nottingham), which sits at the stated max_continuous_h limit with no margin for traffic or rest delays.
Only one break is recorded (14:18–15:03, 45 min) across 8.05 driving hours; the 15:03–17:24 leg is 2h21m continuous, so the break placement is load-bearing for the 4.5h cap.
Two wait periods totalling 69 minutes (06:49–07:05 and 12:12–12:45) are non-productive and are the main source of schedule slack; the 33-minute Nottingham wait is the largest single gap.

The second leg to Reading is split into two drive_loaded segments (32.4 mi then 93.7 mi) around the break, so the 126.1-mile Nottingham→Reading haul is not a single continuous block — worth confirming this reflects a genuine rest stop rather than a split in the leg record.

All four loads considered at the 18:09 Reading decision failed on multiple gates simultaneously (DEADHEAD_TOO_FAR, BELOW_MARGIN_FLOOR, OUT_OF_HOURS, HOME_DEADLINE, MOVES_AWAY_FROM_HOME, plus VEHICLE_MISMATCH on the two Leeds loads and WINDOW_MISSED on two), leaving no viable backhaul and a 48.1-mile empty return leg.
Empty return from Reading costs £109.08 in net terms, so the final leg is loss-making; the day's profitability depends entirely on the two booked loads.

The market restriction summary cites a Peckham High Street traffic order (SE15 5EW) that is marked 'Expired' (published 05/02/26), so it does not currently constrain the 06:45 departure from Peckham, but the notice text is truncated and its expiry date is not confirmed in the evidence.

Diesel at 198.8p/l is near the top of the cited range (197.58–199.33p across sources) and roughly 40% above the year-earlier 142.81p, so fuel cost assumptions are conservative but the cost base is exposed to further increases.

ULEZ charge is recorded as £0.00, which is consistent with a 44t artic routed outside central London, but the plan's route to/from Peckham is not detailed enough to confirm no low-emission or weight-restricted streets are affected.

pricing.summary: T-002 (18t Curtain Side with Tail Lift, driver DRV-002, dispatcher 2) completed a single loaded run from Streatham to Leeds (load 91100018, rate £1,045) and was released at 14:06. The plan is deterministic and fully specified: 1.0 mi deadhead (06:15-06:19), 16 min wait at pickup (06:19-06:35), 45 min load (06:35-07:20), 177.2 mi loaded drive (07:20-11:45), a 45 min break (11:45-12:30), 33.6 mi loaded drive (12:30-13:21) and 45 min unload (13:21-14:06). Totals: 211.7 miles, 5.34 drive hours, 1 break, max continuous 4.5 h, revenue £1,045, cost £456.79, profit £588.21. Baseline for the same day was £165.64 profit with 212.3 empty miles and a 20:08 home time, so the plan is a large improvement on baseline (+£422.57 profit, empty miles cut from 212.3 to 1.0). At 14:06 the truck is free in Leeds with no onward load selected: the STANDARD mode decision is NEEDS_HUMAN with chosen = null, and the empty-return option is infeasible (net -£408.76, home 20:08). All four candidate loads were rejected on feasibility grounds (vehicle mismatch, deadhead distance, wait time, margin floor, and out-of-hours / home-deadline breaches against a 9.0 h driving cap and 21:00 home limit), leaving the run to end with a human decision required. Market inputs are diesel at 198.8p/l, ULEZ charge £0.00, and a TfL A202 Peckham High Street (SE15 5EW) temporary traffic order that is published 05/02/26 and expired, so it does not restrict the 06:15 Streatham deadhead.
risk_flags: ESCALATED status with no chosen load after 14:06: the STANDARD decision returns NEEDS_HUMAN and chosen = null, so the day is left open for manual intervention.
Empty return from Leeds is infeasible: net -£408.76 and home at 20:08, so the truck has no compliant way home under the current plan.

All four evaluated candidate loads are infeasible, each citing OUT_OF_HOURS (11.7h to 14.8h driving needed vs 9.0h cap) and HOME_DEADLINE (home 22:40 to 03:36 vs 21:00 limit); no compliant onward load exists in the evaluated set.
Load 91104875 (Cardiff, £595) rejected for VEHICLE_MISMATCH against the 18t Curtain Side with Tail Lift, plus a 63 min wait and out-of-hours breach.
Load 91101677 (Ipswich, £550) rejected with DEADHEAD_TOO_FAR (49 mi vs 30 mi max) and BELOW_MARGIN_FLOOR (0% vs 8%); net_load_gbp of only £2.65 leaves no economic cushion.
Load 91104146 (Southampton, £550) rejected for BELOW_MARGIN_FLOOR (6.4% vs 8% floor) with net_load_gbp £35.09, so accepting it would be marginal even if hours allowed.
Load 91103609 (Watford, £535) is the closest to viable: net_to_home_gbp +£4.25 and margin 9.9%, but fails on VEHICLE_MISMATCH, DEADHEAD_TOO_FAR (49 mi) and a 22:40 home time.
Max continuous driving of 4.5 h is at the stated limit, with only 1 break recorded; the 45 min break at 11:45-12:30 is the sole rest period in the 5.34 drive hours.

Diesel at 198.8p/l is materially above the ~174-175p/l petrol level and well above the ~142.8p/l paid a year earlier, so fuel cost is the dominant cost driver in the £456.79 cost base and any additional mileage erodes margin quickly.
70 loads were evaluated but only 4 are surfaced in the decision record, so the rejection reasons for the remaining 66 are not visible in this evidence.

The only cited road restriction (TfL A202 Peckham High Street, SE15 5EW) is marked expired, so it provides no current constraint on the Streatham deadhead; no other restrictions are evidenced for the Leeds or return legs.

compliance.summary: T-002 (18t Curtain Side with tail lift, HGV) completed a single booked load 91100018 from Streatham to Leeds, earning £1,045 gross against £456.79 cost for £588.21 profit over 211.7 miles (1.0 empty mile deadhead from home to pickup). The vehicle left home at 06:15, waited 16 minutes at pickup (06:19-06:35), loaded 06:35-07:20, drove 177.2 miles loaded to 11:45, took a 45-minute break, drove a further 33.6 miles to 13:21, and unloaded by 14:06. At 14:06 the dispatcher evaluated 70 candidate loads and selected none: all four shortlisted options were rejected on feasibility grounds (vehicle mismatch, deadhead distance, wait time, below-margin floor, out-of-hours driving cap, and home deadline), and the empty-return leg to Streatham was itself infeasible (net -£408.76, home at 20:08). The plan therefore escalates to NEEDS_HUMAN with no second load booked and no return leg scheduled, leaving the truck's return to base unresolved in the plan. Baseline comparison shows the plan materially outperforms the baseline on profit (£588.21 vs £165.64) and empty miles (1.0 vs 212.3), with an earlier projected home time (20:08 vs 20:08 baseline, same).
risk_flags: ESCALATED status with action NEEDS_HUMAN and chosen=null: no onward load and no return-to-home leg are booked, so the vehicle's return to Streatham is unconfirmed in the plan.
Empty return leg is marked feasible=false with net_gbp -408.76 and home_at 20:08; the return journey is cost-negative and its feasibility is unresolved.

All four shortlisted second-load options are infeasible, three of them primarily on OUT_OF_HOURS (needs 11.7h-14.8h driving vs 9.0h cap) and HOME_DEADLINE (home 22:40 to 03:36 vs 21:00 limit), indicating the 14:06 release from Leeds leaves insufficient legal/plan driving time to return home.
Option 91104875 (Cardiff) and 91103609 (Watford) carry VEHICLE_MISMATCH, so the 18t curtain-side/tail-lift specification does not match those loads' equipment requirements.
Option 91101677 (Ipswich) has DEADHEAD_TOO_FAR (49 mi vs 30 mi max) and BELOW_MARGIN_FLOOR (0% vs 8% floor); 91104146 (Southampton) is BELOW_MARGIN_FLOOR (6.4% vs 8%).
Option 91104875 also has WAIT_TOO_LONG (63 min) at pickup, adding further uncompensated idle time.

max_continuous_h of 4.5h is at/near the 4.5h EU-style driving limit; the 45-minute break at 11:45-12:30 is the only recorded break, and no further breaks are scheduled for the remaining 33.6 miles of loaded driving.
Only 1 break is recorded across 5.34 drive hours, which is consistent with the 4.5h continuous limit but leaves no margin for additional delay before the home deadline.
The 16-minute wait at pickup (06:19-06:35) is uncompensated and is not reflected as a separate cost line.

Market restriction data is a single expired TfL notice for Peckham High Street (SE15 5EW, published 05/02/26, marked Expired) near the Streatham home base; it is not a live restriction and provides no current diversion or closure guidance for the route.
Diesel price inputs vary across cited sources (197.58p to 199.33p/L) versus the 198.8p/L used; the cost figure is sensitive to which weekly average is applied.
ULEZ charge is recorded as 0.0 for the London home area, which is consistent with the 18t vehicle's exemption status but is not independently verified in the evidence.

Baseline empty_miles of 212.3 versus 1.0 in this plan is a very large divergence; the baseline figure is not explained by the recorded events and should be confirmed before being relied on for comparison.
